events.text: You send word to {npc}: a duel, at dawn, on the old threshing floor outside town, before witnesses. {He} sends back one word. Yes.

ok.log: Before the sun is fully up, {npc} is on one knee and the witnesses are very quiet.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you hoped. The witnesses will talk about it for a month.

choices.text: Send word that you have changed your mind

effects.log: You withdraw the challenge. Some of the witnesses laugh, quietly, and you hear them.

events.text: Your challenge reaches {npc} at a teahouse, read aloud by the messenger so that the whole room hears it. {He} puts down {his} cup and names the place: the river bank, at noon.

ok.log: At noon the river bank is yours, and {npc} is down in the reeds.

fail.log: At noon {npc} is the one standing. You walk home along the bank alone.

effects.log: Noon passes, and the teahouse talks.

events.text: You send {npc} a challenge with no limits written on it: a duel to the death. Witnesses gather at the old shrine. Only one of you is meant to walk away. {He} comes, and does not smile.

ok.log: The fight is long and silent. When it ends, {npc} is on the ground and cannot rise, and everyone waits to see what you will do.

fail.log: It goes the wrong way from the first exchange.
fail.deathCause: a duel to the death with {npc}

choices.text: Call it off before the first exchange

effects.log: You lower your weapon before the first exchange. {npc} looks at you for a long time, and goes. The witnesses do not.

events.text: {npc} accepts your challenge to the death in writing, in a fine hand, and adds at the bottom that {he} has put {his} affairs in order. The meeting is on a bare hill at dusk, with the wind against you both.

ok.log: At dusk, on the bare hill, {npc} falls, and stays down. The wind keeps blowing as if nothing had happened.

fail.log: On the bare hill, {npc} is the stronger.
fail.deathCause: a duel to the death with {npc}

effects.log: You send a letter calling it off. {npc} reads it and burns it, and tells everyone what it said.
